reason: The text fragment (Exodus 2:11-15) is a narrative account of Moses as a grown man witnessing the burdens of the Hebrews, killing an Egyptian who struck a Hebrew, and subsequently fleeing Egypt to Midian. While the text references 'Hebrews' (עִבְרִי) as an ethnic/national group, it contains no discussion of what defines or constitutes the Hebrew people as a collective entity, nor does it mention Yahweh, worship, or any theological statement about Hebrew identity. The passage is concerned with historical narrative events, not with theological claims about Hebrew peoplehood.
